description: A single .NET global tool that drives C# services on AWS — bootstrap, deploy, and rollback for Lambda, ECS Fargate, static-site, and coupled full-stack targets, all from one committed manifest.
releaseNotes:
- `kanject run` lists and runs the scripts a repository declares (proposal 0060 P1).
  A repository's developer scripts (a guarded smoke run, a VM test run, a rule check) were found by reading a folder or a house-rules file, and what each one needs showed only when it ran. A repository now names them in `kanject-cli/scripts.json`, and one command answers "what can I run here, and how?" in every Kanject repository, including library repositories with no manifest.
  - `kanject run` lists the scripts with their descriptions and, where one takes arguments, the full invocation (`kanject run smoke -- <apphost> <scratch-dir> <seconds>`). A script that cannot run on this operating system is still listed, marked with the one it needs.
  - `kanject run <NAME> [-- <ARGS>]` starts one with the terminal's own input and output and exits with the script's exit code. Arguments after `--` reach the script as separate arguments, unchanged: `run` is an argument list, not a shell string.
  - `--explain` shows the resolved program, the argument list and what each requirement resolved to, without running anything. `--cwd <DIR>` starts the search elsewhere; the nearest scripts file up to the git root wins.
  - Coded refusals before anything starts, `KANCLI1000`–`KANCLI1005`, the first codes of a new band from 1000: an invalid file, an unknown name (with the nearest one suggested), the wrong operating system, a tool that is not on `PATH`, an unsafe argument to a batch file on Windows, and a program that cannot be started. All six exit 125, so a caller can tell "the script never started" from a script's own exit code. This is the one command where a coded failure does not exit 1.
  - Cancelling lets the script clean up. Ctrl+C reaches the script from the terminal and the CLI waits for it; a termination sent to the CLI alone is passed on. Only after 30 seconds, or on a second Ctrl+C, does the CLI end the process tree, and it says so (exit 130 or 143).
  - A bare program name is looked up on `PATH` only, never in the current folder, and the CLI starts the absolute path it resolved.
  - Nothing else reads the file. No other command and no generated git hook starts a script, and an older CLI never sees `scripts.json`. `kanject doctor` does not validate it yet, and there is no editor schema or name completion.
  - The batch-file rule on Windows (`KANCLI1004`) is built from documented Windows behaviour and has not been run on a Windows machine yet.
